---
title: Getting started
description: Install cadjoint, build a first model, and take a gradient through it.
---

cadjoint is code-first CAD in which sketches, constraints, SDF geometry,
meshing and finite-element simulation compose into one function JAX can
differentiate end to end. This page installs it, builds one model, takes one
gradient, and links to the guide for each stage.

::: {.callout-warning}
The API is not stable. Expect breaking changes.
:::

## Install

From PyPI, pinned because the API moves:

```bash
pip install "cadjoint==<version>"
```

From a checkout, with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/andrinr/cadjoint
cd cadjoint
uv sync                      # CPU JAX: macOS, Linux, Windows
uv sync --extra cuda         # Linux + NVIDIA GPU instead
```

`uv sync` creates `.venv` and installs cadjoint into it in editable mode. Run
commands through it with `uv run <cmd>`, or activate it with
`source .venv/bin/activate`. Everything beyond the geometry core is an extra,
one `--extra` per name (`uv sync --extra fem --extra tesseract --extra viewer`);
the [extras table](https://github.com/andrinr/cadjoint#install) lists what
each pulls in.

`fem` is the one extra that compiles. petsc4py publishes no wheels, so
`uv sync --extra fem` builds PETSc from source and needs a C compiler, gfortran
and BLAS/LAPACK headers (`apt install build-essential gfortran libopenblas-dev`
on Debian/Ubuntu). Without that toolchain, run the solvers as Tesseracts
instead: their images get PETSc from conda-forge and are published prebuilt to
GHCR for amd64 and arm64, so Docker is the only requirement (see
[prebuilt images](plugins.qmd#prebuilt-images)).

### Supported platforms

| Platform | `uv sync` | `uv sync --extra fem` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux x86_64 | yes | compiles PETSc |
| Linux ARM64 | yes | no: gmsh has no Linux ARM wheel |
| macOS arm64 | yes | compiles PETSc |
| macOS x86_64 (Intel) | no: jaxlib has no Intel-Mac wheel for Python 3.11+ | no |
| Windows x86_64 | yes | no: PETSc does not build natively |

Every "yes" is a fresh `uv sync --locked` and `import cadjoint` in
[`install.yml`](https://github.com/andrinr/cadjoint/blob/main/.github/workflows/install.yml),
run on each push. Where the `fem` column says no, the prebuilt solver
Tesseracts run the same solvers in Docker.

## A first model

A four-vertex sketch with one distance constraint, extruded by a free depth
and dual-contoured into a mesh:

```python
from cadjoint.construction import PolygonProfile, SketchPlane, extrude
from cadjoint.constraints import DistanceConstraint, satisfy_constraints
from cadjoint.geometry import Scalar, Vector2
from cadjoint.meshing import GridSpec, extract_mesh, save_stl

a = Vector2([0.0, 0.0], free=True, name="a")
b = Vector2([1.0, 0.0], free=True, name="b")
c = Vector2([1.0, 1.0], free=True, name="c")
d = Vector2([0.0, 1.0], free=True, name="d")
DistanceConstraint(a, b, 1.2)

depth = Scalar(0.5, free=True, name="depth")
block = extrude(PolygonProfile([a, b, c, d], plane=SketchPlane()), depth=depth)
satisfy_constraints(block)          # projects a and b onto the constraint, in place

grid = GridSpec.from_bounds((-0.5, -0.5, -0.5), (2.0, 2.0, 1.5), 32)
mesh = extract_mesh(block, grid)
save_stl(mesh, "block.stl")
```

Parameters, sketches, features and constraints are covered in
[Modelling](modelling.qmd); the mesher and its exporters in
[Meshing](meshing.qmd).

## Gradients

`extract_parameters` splits the tree into free and fixed parameter dicts, and
`functionalize` turns it into a pure function of them. `jax.grad` of anything
downstream reaches every free parameter:

```python
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from cadjoint import extract_parameters, functionalize

free, fixed, _ = extract_parameters(block)
field = functionalize(block)
probe = jnp.array([0.5, 0.5, 0.5])

grads = jax.grad(lambda params: field(params, fixed)(probe))(free)
grads["depth"]      # -0.5: the top cap sits at depth/2
```

The probe lies above the top cap, so only `depth` moves its distance; the
vertex gradients there are zero.

[Optimization](optimization.qmd) runs this gradient through a mesh and a
finite-element solve.

## Playground

The browser app ships in the package and needs the `viewer` extra (`editor`
adds lint and completion):

```bash
uvx --from "cadjoint[viewer,editor]" cadjoint-viewer --open   # nothing installed
uv run --extra viewer --extra editor cadjoint-viewer --open   # from a checkout
```

It opens on a parametric heat sink that declares a mesh, a thermal study and
an optimization. See [the playground](viewer.qmd).

## Scripts

Run from the repository root with `python examples/<name>.py`.

- [`fem_bracket_optimization.py`](https://github.com/andrinr/cadjoint/blob/main/examples/fem_bracket_optimization.py):
  shape optimization of an L-bracket through SDF, hex mesh and linear elastic
  solve (jax-fem or CalculiX), minimizing compliance and mass with Adam;
  writes a convergence CSV, a plot and VTK files to `examples/output/`.
  Requires the `fem` extra and `optax`.
- [`rendering_gallery.py`](https://github.com/andrinr/cadjoint/blob/main/examples/rendering_gallery.py):
  renders the lighting-mode and quality-preset comparison images in
  [Rendering](rendering.qmd) to `docs/assets/`.
